summary: Answer: maybe. Scientists think odd orbits of distant icy worlds hint at an unseen planet 5 to 10 times Earth's mass, but nobody has ever seen it. Pluto sits ~5.5 light-hours away, demoted in 2006 and visited by New Horizons in 2015. Next stop: interstellar space.

scenes.narration: Is a ninth planet hiding out here?
The answer: maybe. Nobody has ever seen it.
Past Neptune lies the Kuiper Belt, a ring of icy leftovers.
Pluto lives here, about five and a half light-hours away.
In two thousand six, astronomers demoted it to a dwarf planet.
Then in twenty fifteen, New Horizons found mountains of ice there.
Astronomers noticed distant icy worlds all swinging the same strange way.
Scientists think a massive planet might be tugging them, five to ten times Earth's mass.
Its orbit could last ten thousand to twenty thousand years.
Yet no telescope has ever spotted it. It might not exist at all.
